What is Anyword?

AI copywriting platform whose distinguishing feature is predictive performance scoring - every piece of generated copy receives a predicted performance score based on a model trained on billions of marketing messages and their actual results.

Best for

Choosing between copy variants using data rather than opinion.

Main features

  • Predictive Performance Score on every generated variant
  • Custom Scoring Models trained on your own historical campaign data
  • Brand Voice and messaging framework enforcement
  • Blog Wizard for long-form
  • Data-Driven Copy across ads, email, landing pages and social
  • Copy Intelligence analysing which of your existing messages performed best
  • competitor messaging analysis
  • audience-specific variants
  • Chrome extension writing in any tool.

Practical use cases

  • Choosing between ten ad headline variants using a predicted score rather than a hunch
  • training a scoring model on your own conversion data
  • enforcing messaging consistency across a large marketing team
  • analysing which existing copy actually performed and why.

Who is it for?

  • Performance marketers, demand-generation teams, copywriters at scale and marketing operations teams.

Pricing, free access & limits

Per-seat subscription with word/credit allowances

Plans described in the source

Starter around $39/mo ($49 monthly) for 1 seat with basic scoring. Data-Driven around $79-99/seat/mo with custom scoring models and Copy Intelligence. Business around $349/mo with multiple seats, custom models and API. Enterprise custom, annual, with dedicated models, SSO and support. Annual billing roughly 20-25% cheaper. Anyword removed its free tier some years ago.

Free plan

No free plan.

Free trial

Yes - 7-day free trial with limited words.

Usage limits to consider

Word or credit allowances per tier. Custom Scoring Models require the Data-Driven tier and enough historical data to train on. Seat counts tier-limited.

Strengths & tradeoffs

These points summarize the supplied research, rather than hands-on test results.

Strengths noted in the source

  • The predictive scoring is the most defensible claim in the AI copywriting category - it is trained on real performance data rather than being a generic model with marketing language
  • Custom Scoring Models trained on your own results are genuinely valuable for mature teams with data
  • Copy Intelligence analysing your historical performance is a useful diagnostic nobody else offers as cleanly.

Limitations to consider

  • Expensive relative to generic writing tools, and the premium only pays off if you act on the scores
  • custom scoring models need substantial historical data, which smaller teams lack
  • the scoring methodology is proprietary and unaudited
  • raw copy quality is comparable to frontier models, not better
  • no free tier makes evaluation commitment-heavy
  • the interface is dated.

Platforms, languages & integrations

Platforms

  • Web, Chrome extension
  • API on higher tiers

Languages

  • 30+ languages including Arabic and French

API access

Yes - on Business and Enterprise tiers

Integrations and exports

  • Google Ads, Meta Ads, LinkedIn, HubSpot, Salesforce, Google Docs, Notion, WordPress, Chrome (any web text field)

Evaluation notes

The custom scoring model is the feature that justifies the price - without enough of your own performance data to train it, you are paying a premium for a generic score. Validate predicted scores against your own A/B test results before changing how you allocate budget.
